# Disposable pilot-scope test fixtures

The seed and HTTP client are synthetic and must only run against a fresh disposable database. The caller-settable `forms.pilot_fixture` marker is an accident guard, not authorization; the HTTP script accepts only a disposable loopback endpoint and uses a public test JWT key. No real owner or approval is included.

For local PGlite run `node --test supabase/tests/forms-pilot-scope.test.mjs`. The PostgREST fixture requires disposable PostgreSQL and PostgREST with HTP migrations 000–009, quota 28 and `20261201000000_forms_pilot_scope.sql`; apply the seed in a session with `forms.pilot_fixture=disposable`. Configure PostgREST with the synthetic key in `postgrest-check.mjs`. Set `PILOT_FIXTURE=disposable` and `PILOT_FIXTURE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`. The `held8` and `service_acl` phases check default holds; after a disposable regrant the `all8` and `concurrent` phases exercise direct owner RPCs. The `revoked` and `reapproved` phases check the same submission ID before and after removing approval. These synthetic regrants and approvals are not instructions for a hosted target.

The PG17/PostgREST fixture substitutes synthetic `auth.jwt()` and `auth.uid()` helpers; it cannot verify deployed authentication or claims. `scripts/test-forms-pilot-http.sh` starts disposable PG17/PostgREST containers bound to loopback, runs the actual API/browser fixture for initially unapproved, approved and revoked states, checks direct owner/service denials and removes its containers and temporary files. It requires Docker, Node, Rust, OpenSSL and Playwright Chromium; it fails if the ignored Rust test is skipped or cleanup cannot be verified. CI runs this script explicitly. Its synthetic Fly header does not verify a real proxy path. Release, fail-closed disable, administrator, cleanup and scheduler limits are documented in `docs/forms/pilot-scope-migration.md`.
